static_vignette: A 40-year-old female presents with 3 weeks of migratory joint pain, facial drooping on the left, and heart palpitations. She went camping in Connecticut 5 weeks ago and noticed a bull's-eye rash on her thigh 4 weeks ago that she initially ignored. Her EKG shows 2nd degree AV block Mobitz type II.

critical_facts: erythema migrans history confirmed Lyme endemic area
bilateral facial palsy is Lyme until proven otherwise
red_flags: complete AV block with hemodynamic compromise
unsafe_actions: pace permanently without treating Lyme first
not treat Lyme carditis with IV antibiotics
oral doxycycline only for 3rd degree AV block Lyme carditis

correct_management: IV ceftriaxone 2g daily for carditis with high-degree AV block
temporary pacing if HR <40 or symptomatic
transition to oral doxycycline when AV block resolves
